name: The episodic memory's stores at pixel scale, keyed on the senses and on the cortex
question: With Brain.compose(12824, 75, modules=(512,), arousal=True, memory_choice=True): how many bytes do the episodic memory's stores and separators hold under memory_key="sensory" and "cortex", and what does a live moment cost on random inputs?
scope: storage and work of the library's episodic memory at a pixel-sized input; random inputs carry no task, so nothing here measures behavior

brain.note: 75 motor neurons in one slot; every other setting at the composed founder with the episodic memory's defaults

life.observations: each moment a fresh (1, 12824) row of uniform values in [0, 1) from numpy.random.default_rng(12824)
life.rewards: from the same generator after each observation: +1 below .1, -1 from .1 to .2, else 0; the first moment has none; no done
life.refusals: a refused moment is counted and the life continues with the next observation and no reward

readings: bytes of each store before and after the life: separator projection and mean, strength, consolidated, mass
checkpoint file bytes after the life
wall seconds per live call: mean, median, 90th percentile, over all moments and over routine and aroused moments
seconds and calls in the stores' reads (recall) and writes (observe)
free-solve and learning sweeps per moment, routine moments, refusals
peak resident memory of the process
procedure: each key in its own process, one after the other, one BLAS thread, on a machine shared with other work; wall times are indicative
report: a table of bytes per store and key, and a table of time per decision per key
